title: Knowing the Assembly
note: He defines this as knowing the nature of the assembly around the ruler. When you speak on business you need this as well as reading his mind.

couplets.plain: Those pure in speech, who know the range of words, should know the assembly, weigh it up, and then speak.
couplets.pm: Those with the purity of knowing the whole body of words, plain, figurative and suggestive, should drop what doesn’t suit them. Before speaking they should measure the assembly against themselves, as higher, equal or lower, and weigh what to say there, how to say it and where it will lead.

links.quote: know the assembly, weigh it up, and then speak
links.reason: Tells the skilled speaker to study the assembly and weigh it before saying anything.

links.quote: who know the range of words
links.reason: Calls directly on those who know the range of words and must stand before a gathering.

couplets.plain: Those good at the ways of words should judge the moment, understand it well, and then speak.
couplets.pm: Those with the goodness of having studied how words work should, when they speak in an assembly, find the right moment and speak very clearly, without error. How words work is how each kind yields its meaning. The moment is when the hearers want to listen. Errors are of word and of meaning.

links.reason: Puts judging the moment ahead of any speech, however good the speaker.

links.quote: good at the ways of words
links.reason: Calls directly on those who have studied the ways of words.

couplets.plain: Those who take on speaking without knowing the assembly don’t know the kinds of speech, and have no skill at all.
couplets.pm: Those who take on speaking without knowing the measure of the assembly don’t know the kinds of speech, because speech varies with what the hearers can grasp. They have no learned skill either, because everyone scorns them for this ignorance.

links.quote: take on speaking without knowing the assembly

couplets.plain: Be bright before the bright. Before the blank, take on the colour of white lime.
couplets.pm: Before those bright in understanding, your superiors and equals, be bright yourself, and set out your learning and eloquence at length. The petty, who can’t judge an assembly, he calls white, after timber with no heartwood. Before them take on the colour of white lime: be blanker than they are, so that they think well of you.

links.reason: Fits you to the hearers: bright before the bright, and blank as white lime before the blank.

links.quote: Before the blank, take on the colour of white lime
links.reason: Advises not spending your brightness on those who can’t take it in, only going as blank as they are.

couplets.plain: Better even than all that is called good is the restraint of not speaking first among elders.
couplets.pm: Of all the qualities praised as good, the best is the restraint of not speaking ahead of those greater than you in an assembly. You know your own lack, their greatness, the disgrace of speaking first and the good of holding back. Only speaking first is forbidden, so you may speak with them or after them.

links.quote: the restraint of not speaking first among elders

couplets.plain: Stumbling before those who have taken in wide learning is like losing your footing on the path.
couplets.pm: When a skilled speaker’s words slip in the assembly of those who take in wide learning and know its truth, it is like someone on the good path to liberation losing his footing and falling, a person who guarded his five senses and then fell into false conduct. He loses the reward and is scorned as well.

couplets.plain: The learning of the well-read shines among those who can weigh words without fault.
couplets.pm: If they speak in the assembly of those who can examine words without fault, the learning of those who have studied many books and grasped what they yield shines out for everyone. So speak there.

links.quote: shines among those who can weigh words without fault
links.reason: Learning shines out before hearers able to weigh words without fault.
Concerns the scholar, whose learning shines among those who can weigh words.

couplets.plain: To speak before those with understanding is like pouring water on a bed where something is already growing.
couplets.pm: When a learned person speaks in the assembly of those who can understand things unaided, it is like pouring water on a bed where a crop grows by itself. Learning that would grow anyway grows greatly. So among your equals, speak by every means.

links.quote: To speak before those with understanding
links.reason: Speech given to those who can take it in feeds them, as water feeds what is already growing.

links.quote: pouring water on a bed where something is already growing
links.reason: Speaking to people of understanding is water poured on a bed of growing plants.

couplets.plain: If you can speak so that a good assembly takes it in, don’t speak in a petty one, even by forgetting.
couplets.pm: Those fit to say good things so that the good take them in should not, even by forgetting, say them among the petty. If they do, the good assembly scorns them for not knowing their audience, and the petty one scorns them too, because it can’t follow the matter. They become fit for neither.

links.quote: don’t speak in a petty one, even by forgetting
links.reason: Warns those who speak well before a good assembly not to speak in a petty one, even by forgetting.

links.quote: speak so that a good assembly takes it in
links.reason: Calls directly on those who can make a good assembly take in what they say.

couplets.plain: Speaking before those not of your own kind is like ambrosia spilled in a filthy yard.
couplets.pm: Say nothing at all before those who aren’t of your own kind, the good. If you do, it is ambrosia spilled in an unclean yard: the medicine against death, wasted, reaching no one who would enjoy it. Such speech is useless. He rejects the reading that likens the act of speaking to ambrosia, because an act can’t match a thing.

links.quote: before those not of your own kind
links.reason: Speaking before those not of your own kind is pure waste, so a speaker must pick the hearers.

links.quote: ambrosia spilled in a filthy yard
links.reason: Talk before those not of your own kind is the sweetest thing there is, lost in a filthy yard.
